sections.lever checks:
- Platform document numbers: local ids follow alphabetical file names. Here D02 = Doc 1, D07 = Doc 7 and D12 = Doc 12; the full mapping is in notes/doc-map.md. Reasoning uses platform numbers.
- Family and target: letter timeline of one commenter across three documents, with the latest letter shown only by its name in another group's signature block (hook h1, sketch i02); target medium per the user's instruction of 2026-10-12 ("there is no slot for Easy Tier for this bundle, we should target medium and high"). Built on the measured family result of aq-03170 q01 rev 3 (a commenter's letter shown only in another commenter's text, Low 0/5 · Medium 1/5). Measured platform result for this question pending.
- Dependency plan: D02 l15 (comments on the ESG disclosure rule submitted August 16, 2022) -> D02 l3 and l9 (supplemental comments of November 1, 2022, File Nos. S7-10-22 and S7-17-22) -> D07 l3, l9 and l14 (supplemental letter of October 19, 2023, File No. S7-17-22) -> D12 l3, l8-l9, l12 and l131 (coalition letter of April 16, 2024, File No. S7-17-22, Sierra Club among the signers) -> gaps 77, 352 and 180 days -> 609 / 3 = 203. Minimal inputs: one date and one letter from each of D02, D07 and D12, plus the August 16, 2022 date (in D02 and in D07).
- Universe: every mention of the Sierra Club in the twelve texts (grep "Sierra Club", case-insensitive): D02 l9, l11, l15, l83 (its November 1, 2022 letter and signers); D07 l13, l88 (its October 19, 2023 letter); D11 l67 and l129 (its petition for review of the climate rule, filed March 13, 2024: a court filing, not a comment letter); D12 l131 (signature block of the April 16, 2024 letter). No mention in D01, D03, D04, D05, D06, D08, D09 or D10. Letters on the fund ESG disclosure proposal: four. Excluded: the June 16, 2022 comments (D02 l15), which are on the climate risk disclosure rule only.
- Necessity: D02 is the only document that shows the November 1, 2022 letter (D07 names only the August 16, 2022 comments, l14); without it there are three letters and the mean is 609 / 2 = 304.5. D07 is the only document that shows the October 19, 2023 letter; without it there are three letters and the mean is again 304.5. D12 is the only document that shows the April 16, 2024 letter and the Sierra Club's signature on it; without it there are three letters and the mean is 429 / 2 = 214.5. The August 16, 2022 date is printed in both D02 and D07, so neither is needed for that date, but each supplies a letter the other does not. No mandatory model removal probes.
- Selected-lever checks: who belongs where: the April 16, 2024 letter is led by another organisation and the Sierra Club appears only as a signer; counted, the mean is 203, left out it is 214.5. Bury one list item late: that signer line is at the end of the last document (D12 l131 of 143 lines). Calculate across documents: four dates from three documents. Other wrong routes, not declared as traps: only the two letters in hand, 352; the November 1, 2022 letter left out as a climate-rule letter, 304.5 (D02's heading and first sentence place it on both rules); the August 16, 2022 comments left out, 532 / 2 = 266; the June 16, 2022 climate comments wrongly added, 670 / 4 = 167.5.
- Targeted failure modes: one declared. Linking across documents / Wrong members in a list: the letter set stops at three because the fourth is linked to the Sierra Club only by its name in D12's signature block; wrong answer 214.5 days (77 + 352 = 429; 429 / 2), recomputed by script. Not yet measured on this question. Considered and not declared: Superseded date or version (the October 2023 letter taken as the latest), which describes the same miss and whose platform definition is not on record.
- Calculation verification (caller script, Python datetime, 2026-10-12, scratchpad dates.py): August 16, 2022 -> November 1, 2022 = 77; -> October 19, 2023 = 352; -> April 16, 2024 = 180; total 609; 609 / 3 = 203.0. Elapsed days, end minus start; 2024 is a leap year (February 29 falls inside the third gap). The mean is an exact integer, so no rounding is involved.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no text prints 203, 609, 180, 352 or 77 as a day count (grep for each as a whole number: none in D02, D07 or D12 besides page and footnote markers). The capture's overview lists the four dates under Doc 1, Doc 7 and Doc 12 but does not name the Sierra Club under Doc 12 (its names there are the lead signer, the SEC, its Secretary, GFANZ, JP Morgan Asset Management and BlackRock). Shortest complete route: the three documents above.
- Precision/readings: each date is printed once per letter and the August 16, 2022 date agrees in D02 and D07. "Days ... separated" is elapsed days; inclusive counting would give 612 / 3 = 204 and is not what "separated" asks. "Through April 2024" closes the period at the bundle's last letter; letters outside the bundle cannot be known from it.
- Completeness: intake.json records no gaps. The known visual gaps (D02 l59 CDP table, D04 l213 surveyed-owner finding, D10 figure values) carry no letter date or signature.
- Style/set review: one ask, 24 words, plain wording; "fund ESG disclosure proposal" is a paraphrase (the letters say "ESG Disclosure Proposal", "ESG disclosure rule" and "Fund ESG Proposal"). First question on this bundle; sketches i01, i03 and i04 share this hook's family and would not be submitted beside it.

sections.question: Counting co-signed letters, how many days on average separated consecutive Sierra Club comment letters on the SEC's fund ESG disclosure proposal through April 2024?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 1, date line, heading and footnote 1): the Sierra Club's supplemental comments of November 1, 2022 are filed on both the climate risk disclosure rule and the ESG disclosure rule (File Nos. S7-10-22 and S7-17-22). Footnote 1 says its comments on the ESG disclosure rule were submitted on August 16, 2022, so that earlier letter is the first one and this is the second.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 7, date line, subject line and opening paragraph): the Sierra Club wrote again on October 19, 2023 about the same proposal, File No. S7-17-22. It calls that letter a supplement to the comments it submitted on August 16, 2022 and does not mention the November letter.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 12, date line, opening paragraph and signature block): the letter of April 16, 2024 on the same proposal is from Americans for Financial Reform Education Fund and the organizations signed below it. The Sierra Club is one of those signers, so this is a letter it co-signed and it counts.

Step 4. Application (Doc 1, Doc 7 and Doc 12): no other Sierra Club comment letter on this proposal appears through April 2024. In date order the letters are August 16, 2022, then November 1, 2022, then October 19, 2023, then April 16, 2024, which leaves three gaps between one letter and the next. A count that stops at the Sierra Club's own letters, or at what the October letter says about earlier comments, misses the last one.

Step 5. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 7): August has 31 days, so after August 16 it has this many left: 31 - 16 = 15

Step 6. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 7): the first gap, adding September, October and November 1: 15 + 30 + 31 + 1 = 77

Step 7. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 7): days from November 1, 2022 to October 1, 2023, taking the months from November to September in turn: 30 + 31 + 31 + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 30 = 334

Step 8. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 7): days from October 1 to October 19: 19 - 1 = 18

Step 9. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 7): the second gap, from November 1, 2022 to October 19, 2023: 334 + 18 = 352

Step 10. Calculation (Doc 7 and Doc 12): October has 31 days, so after October 19 it has this many left: 31 - 19 = 12

Step 11. Calculation (Doc 7 and Doc 12): 2024 is a leap year, so the days in its February are: 28 + 1 = 29

Step 12. Calculation (Doc 7 and Doc 12): the third gap, adding November, December, January, February, March and 16 days of April: 12 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 29 + 31 + 16 = 180

Step 13. Calculation (Doc 1, Doc 7 and Doc 12): the three gaps together, in days: 77 + 352 + 180 = 609

Step 14. Final answer (Doc 1, Doc 7 and Doc 12): the average gap between consecutive letters, in days: 609 / 3 = 203
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

Why these are traps: Linking across documents: the Sierra Club's name sits in the signature block of Doc 12's April 16, 2024 coalition letter, while Doc 7 names only its August 16, 2022 comments. Leaving that letter out gives three letters and 214.5 days; all four letters give 203.
